questions.question: Explain the difference between financial and non-financial motivation, giving two examples of each.

points.text: Financial motivation involves monetary rewards: wages (paid per hour worked), salaries (fixed annual amount), commission (percentage of sales achieved), bonuses (one-off performance payments). Non-financial motivation involves non-monetary rewards: job enrichment (more challenging work), empowerment (decision-making authority), job rotation (variety of tasks), fringe benefits like flexible working

questions.question: Describe how Maslow's hierarchy of needs can help a business understand what motivates its employees.

points.text: Maslow's hierarchy shows needs in order: physiological (basic pay for food/shelter) → safety (job security, safe conditions) → social (teamworking, belonging) → esteem (recognition, promotion) → self-actualisation (fulfilling potential). questions.question: Evaluate whether a business should focus more on financial rewards or non-financial methods to motivate staff.

points.text: Financial rewards: attract and retain staff, meet basic needs, easily measured and compared, but can be expensive and their motivational effect fades (people adapt to higher pay). Non-financial methods: lower cost, address higher-level needs, create lasting motivation and job satisfaction, but harder to implement, vary between individuals, and won't work if basic pay is inadequate. markScheme.exemplarAnswer: A grade 9 response will: identify problems (repetitive work, low pay, high targets, lack of progression); financial solutions (competitive salary, attendance bonuses, performance commission); non-financial solutions (job rotation between campaigns, team competitions, empowerment to resolve customer issues without escalation, clear promotion path, social events); apply Herzberg (pay rise = hygiene factor, reduces dissatisfaction but doesn't motivate long-term); apply Maslow (once basic pay is adequate, social and esteem needs become more important); conclude: a balanced approach is needed - raise pay to competitive levels first, then implement non-financial methods (empowerment, progression, team belonging) for sustained motivation and retention.
